pr_title: soc: esp32c6: fix wifi by proper interrupt handling
pr_body:
Current interrupt allocator is not taking into account reserved areas.
In case of esp32c6, Wi-Fi isn't properly configured, causing instability or even non-functional feature.
This adds the reserved area ranges for all risc-v based SoC and unify the slot finding based on interrupt source.
This also fix the scenario where Wi-Fi is disconnected and esp_wifi_send() is called.

Fixes #86258
Fixes #85466
Fixes #83784
pr_comments: This fix some issues regarding esp32c6 Wi-Fi. Will confirm whether the ranges are fully correct.
I can confirm that this fixes the issue I reported here; https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/86258
hey, tagging 4.2, bit too big for this stage, let's backport it once 4.0 is released

@fabiobaltieri We have another PR that refactors ESP32 interrupt allocator for both riscv and xtensa in a single manager. That PR will be submitted after 4.1 release. This PR addresses esp32c6 Wi-Fi issues and is intended only for this release. I know it is a bit late now but was worth submitting anyway. I have to think whether we can/should backport it later or not. Will check.

Hey, been pointed out that the issue that this fixes is actually a regression that has been introduced in this cycle (https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/83213 apparently), plus it's all very well isolated to Risc-V family, so with those in mind I now think this should be merged before the release. @kartben what do you think? @martinjaeger can you unblock? I really don't want to delay this further at this point.
Will update this one to change as minimal as possible to have those issues fixed.
@martinjaeger I only skip renaming files and Kconfig, just maintaining as it has been.

issue_context.title: ESP32-C6: Enabling CONFIG_WATCHDOG=y breaks WiFi
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**

As the title indicates. Wifi works normally on ESP32-C6, unless setting CONFIG_WATCHDOG=y, which if set results in no wifi communications. Router log indicates no activity.


**To Reproduce**

Any wifi sample; set CONFIG_WATCHDOG=y


**Expected behavior**

Using the watchdog timer should not break wifi.


**Impact**

showstopper


**Logs and console output**

From samples/net/wifi/apsta_mode with the following patch for C6;
